[LCCO.6.2] The constraint expression has the same grammar and
typing rules as a `where` clause. `response` is a bound name
referring to the response fact, so `response.<slot>` reads a slot of the service's
response schema ([LCRS.5.5]). The clause's body sees the same fact under the same
name, as an `error` body sees `error` ([LCCO.8.4]).

Each name is bound in the body of the clause that matched it, and not in a
continuation of a call made inside that body ([LCCO.10.1]), which sees the rule's
LHS bindings ([LCCO.10.3]) and its own `response` or `error`. The compiler **must**
refuse a read of an enclosing clause's fact as an unknown binding
(`DS_VALIDATE_UNKNOWN_BINDING`).
